title: Whether constructors can be static, final, or abstract
answer: No. Constructors cannot be declared `static`, `final`, or `abstract`. They initialize instances, are not inherited or overridden, and must have an implementation when declared. Therefore `static` conflicts with instance construction, `final` is unnecessary because constructors cannot be overridden, and `abstract` conflicts with the requirement that construction execute concrete initialization logic.
